events.title: DOGE used flawed AI prompts to cancel Veterans Affairs contracts
events.summary: The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) used AI prompts to identify and "munch" (cancel) contracts related to the Department of Veterans' Affairs. DOGE employee Sahil Lavingia, who worked for two months, stated the goal was to target contracts not "directly supporting patient care." However, the code was deeply flawed, producing wildly inaccurate contract valuations and fundamental misunderstandings of what the contracts actually accomplished. Lavingia acknowledged "mistakes were made."
events.why_relevant: Use of defective automated systems to cancel government contracts affecting veterans' services demonstrates reckless governance and potential harm to a vulnerable population without adequate review or understanding of consequences.
events.basis: the AI prompts the Department of Government Efficiency used to 'munch'—the word DOGE employee Sahil Lavingia used for 'cancel'—contracts related to the Department of Veterans' Affairs. But the code was deeply flawed, resulting in wildly off-base contract values.

events.summary: Dr. Rupa Marya, an internal medicine physician and professor at UCSF, filed a lawsuit alleging the university violated her First Amendment free speech rights by suspending her in September 2024 and subsequently terminating her employment. The suspension followed her social media posts criticizing Zionism as a "supremacist, racist ideology" and expressing solidarity with Palestinian healthcare workers. UCSF published a statement condemning her remarks as a "racist conspiracy theory." Marya's attorney argues her posts never impeded her duties and that she was denied a hearing to which she was entitled.

events.title: DOJ dismisses felony charges against LA immigration protesters after false federal agent testimony
events.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice dismissed at least eight felony charges against Los Angeles protesters arrested during June 2025 immigration demonstrations after discovering that Department of Homeland Security agents made false and misleading statements in their reports. Federal prosecutors filed charges against at least 26 people for assaulting and impeding federal officers, but video evidence contradicted agent testimony about the sequence of events and who initiated physical contact. The dismissals represent a major embarrassment for Trump-appointed U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli and reflect systemic failures in case vetting and officer accountability.
events.why_relevant: The dismissals expose how federal law enforcement fabricated evidence against protesters exercising First Amendment rights, then prosecutors filed charges without adequate scrutiny, demonstrating weaponization of the justice system to suppress dissent and instill fear.
events.basis: US immigration officers made false and misleading statements in their reports about several Los Angeles protesters they arrested during the massive demonstrations that rocked the city in June, according to federal law enforcement files obtained by the Guardian.

events.title: Trump administration returned wrongfully rendered immigrant to U.S. and charged him
events.summary: After months of maintaining it could not bring back Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Maryland man wrongfully rendered to the CECOT terrorist prison in El Salvador, the Trump administration returned him to the U.S. A grand jury in Tennessee charged Abrego Garcia with participating in a ten-year conspiracy to transport undocumented migrants from Texas to other parts of the country, alleging participation in more than 100 trips involving children and MS-13 gang members. However, the indictment contains significant issues: Abrego Garcia is the only person named in the alleged conspiracy; the investigation began only in April after courts ordered his return; and the indictment is based on a 2022 traffic stop where he was neither ticketed nor charged at the time. The chief of the criminal division for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Nashville, Ben Schrader, resigned on May 21, the same day as the indictment, citing concerns the case was being pursued for political reasons.
events.why_relevant: The return of a wrongfully rendered person followed by a questionable indictment with apparent political motivation, combined with a prosecutor's resignation citing political concerns, raises serious questions about rule of law and weaponization of the justice system.

events.summary: On Saturday, June 7, President Trump authorized deployment of 2,000 national guard troops to Los Angeles and federalized them under Title 10 authority, placing them under federal rather than state control. The deployment followed two days of mass protests against Immigration and Customs Enforcement raids in downtown LA and Paramount. California Governor Gavin Newsom condemned the mobilization as "purposefully inflammatory" and stated no unmet law enforcement need existed. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth threatened to deploy active-duty Marines if unrest continued. Border Patrol used teargas on protesters; dozens were arrested.
events.why_relevant: Federalizing state national guard troops under presidential authority without gubernatorial consent and deploying them against domestic protest constitutes a direct assertion of executive power over state sovereignty and raises constitutional questions about the limits of federal military deployment on U.S. soil.
events.basis: Trump, according to the memo, federalized the state's national guard troops under what is known as Title 10 authority, which places them under federal, rather than state, control.
events.action: federalized national guard and authorized deployment

events.title: Trump federalizes California National Guard over governor's objection
events.summary: President Trump federalized 2,000 California National Guard troops on Saturday without prior notice to Governor Newsom, marking the first time a U.S. president has acted over a state governor's objections in this manner in over 50 years. The deployment was ordered in response to protests over immigration raids in Los Angeles. Newsom characterized the action as unconstitutional, illegal overreach, and "theater," and subsequently filed a request for a restraining order. U.S. Marines were added to support ICE enforcement operations.
events.why_relevant: This represents an extraordinary assertion of federal executive power over state authority, violating the constitutional principle that governors command their own National Guard absent a declared emergency or congressional authorization, and signals potential erosion of federalism and separation of powers.
events.basis: Trump federalized 2,000 of California's national guard on Saturday, with a US president acting over the objections of a state governor in this way for the first time in more than half a century.

events.title: Trump deployed 700 Marines and federalized 4,100 California National Guard personnel in Los Angeles
events.summary: On June 7, Trump deployed 700 Marines to Los Angeles and federalized 4,100 California National Guard personnel following scattered protests of immigration raids. Administration officials claimed troops were not engaged in law enforcement but were protecting federal agents. In a trial held last week, federal government lawyers argued that troops can protect federal agents wherever they go, effectively asserting there are no limits to presidential use of troops domestically despite the 1878 Posse Comitatus Act. The deployment was deeply unpopular; of 72 soldiers whose enlistment expired during the deployment, 55 said they would not extend service, yielding a 21 percent retention rate versus a normal 60 percent rate.
events.why_relevant: Deployment of active-duty military personnel in a state against the governor's wishes and assertion of unlimited presidential authority to use troops domestically directly challenges constitutional limits on executive power and the Posse Comitatus Act.
events.federal_nexus: Trump asserted federal authority to deploy active-duty Marines and federalize state National Guard without state consent, challenging the constitutional division of military authority between federal and state governments.
events.basis: On June 7, Trump deployed 700 Marines to Los Angeles and federalized 4,100 California National Guard personnel after scattered protests of immigration raids.

events.title: DHS blocks Democratic lawmakers from conducting congressional oversight visits to ICE detention facilities
events.summary: Democratic members of Congress have been systematically denied entry to ICE detention facilities across the country to conduct legally mandated oversight inspections. The Trump administration's Department of Homeland Security imposed a policy requiring one week's advance notice for congressional visits, which Democrats argue violates federal law and their constitutional oversight authority. Democratic lawmakers including Representatives Yassamin Ansari, Judy Chu, Jason Crow, and others report being turned away from facilities in Arizona, California, New York, and New Jersey despite their legal right to unannounced inspections under federal statute.
events.why_relevant: This action directly obstructs Congress's constitutional oversight authority and prevents lawmakers from documenting alleged human rights abuses in detention facilities, undermining the separation of powers and checks and balances.
events.basis: From New York to California, Democratic members of Congress have been repeatedly blocked from entering Ice detention facilities where thousands of noncitizens – many with no criminal convictions – are being held.

events.title: Louisiana enacts chemtrail prohibition legislation
events.summary: Louisiana's state house of representatives passed legislation to ban "chemtrails" (aircraft contrails), a nonexistent phenomenon based on conspiracy theory. The bill requires the state department of environmental quality to document reported chemtrail sightings and forward complaints to the Louisiana air national guard. At least eight states, including Florida and Tennessee, have introduced similar geo-engineering or weather-modification legislation. While the Louisiana bill carries no penalties, opponents warn it could be weaponized to force airline reroutes, challenge airport locations, or initiate legal action against carriers.
events.why_relevant: Legislation codifying baseless conspiracy theories into law represents a degradation of evidence-based governance and the normalization of falsehood in democratic institutions.
events.federal_nexus: The legislation targets commercial aviation, a federally regulated industry, and invokes federal agencies (FAA, EPA, NOAA) as implicit adversaries.
events.basis: Louisiana's bill, which must pass through the senate before reaching Governor Jeff Landry's desk, orders the department of environmental quality to record reported chemtrail sightings and pass complaints on to the Louisiana air national guard.

events.title: DHS agent testimony contradicted by video evidence in assault cases against protesters
events.summary: Department of Homeland Security agents filed inaccurate criminal complaints against five Latino U.S. citizen protesters, misrepresenting the sequence of events and who initiated physical contact. Border Patrol Agent Eduardo Mejorado gave inaccurate testimony about the order of arrests; video evidence showed an officer pushing protester Brayan Ramos-Brito rather than the reverse. DHS supervisors later acknowledged errors and apologized, noting "due to the chaos of the events that day, some events may have been miscommunicated." Despite these documented inaccuracies, prosecutors initially charged all five with felony assault carrying potential 20-year sentences before dismissing most charges within two weeks.
events.why_relevant: Systematic falsification of evidence by federal agents against protesters exercising constitutional rights demonstrates institutional failure to police law enforcement misconduct and reveals how fabricated charges are used to detain and intimidate dissidents.

events.title: Trump falsely claims National Guard had already engaged in Los Angeles before arrival
events.summary: At 2:41 a.m. on Sunday, June 9, Trump posted on social media: "Great job by the National Guard in Los Angeles after two days of violence, clashes and unrest." At the time of the post, the National Guard had not yet arrived in Los Angeles. Trump had spent the evening watching three hours of UFC fighting in New Jersey. The National Guard arrived in Los Angeles much later on Sunday morning when streets were already quiet. Trump also asserted without evidence that protesters were "paid troublemakers."
events.why_relevant: The President made a false factual claim about military operations to the public, undermining the credibility of official communications and creating a false narrative about the necessity and effectiveness of the deployment.

events.title: EPA extends TSCA health and safety data reporting deadline to May 22, 2026 for 16 chemical substances
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency issued a final rule extending the submission deadline for manufacturers and importers to report unpublished health and safety studies on 16 specified chemical substances under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) section 8(d). The deadline, previously set at June 11, 2025 (vinyl chloride) and September 9, 2025 (other 15 chemicals), is now unified at May 22, 2026. events.summary: The Food and Drug Administration submitted a proposed information collection to the Office of Management and Budget for review and clearance under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. events.title: President grants presidential permit to Green Corridors, LLC for commercial elevated guideway border crossing near Laredo, Texas
events.summary: The President issued a presidential permit on June 9, 2025, authorizing Green Corridors, LLC to construct, maintain, and operate a commercial elevated guideway crossing at the U.S.-Mexico border near Laredo, Texas. The permit, published in the Federal Register on June 18, 2025, grants authority under 33 U.S.C. 535d and imposes 15 conditions including environmental compliance, federal agency inspection access, coordination with the International Boundary and Water Commission, State Department diplomatic notification, and a five-year construction deadline. The permittee must fund inspection facilities, operations, maintenance, and technology integration for U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
events.why_relevant: Presidential permits for international border infrastructure represent significant exercises of executive authority over cross-border commerce, sovereignty, and infrastructure development with long-term implications for trade and border operations.
events.basis: I hereby grant permission, subject to the conditions set forth herein, to Green Corridors, LLC (the 'permittee'), to construct, maintain, and operate a commercial elevated guideway crossing located on the United States border with Mexico in Laredo, Texas.

events.title: EPA announces SACC peer review meetings for high-priority phthalates risk evaluations
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency announced two virtual public meetings of the Science Advisory Committee on Chemicals (SACC) to peer review draft risk evaluations and technical support documents for five high-priority phthalates (DBP, DCHP, DEHP, BBP, DIBP) under the Toxic Substances Control Act. A preparatory meeting is scheduled for July 21, 2025, and a peer review meeting for August 4–8, 2025. EPA solicited public comments on draft documents by July 25, 2025, with oral comments due by specified deadlines. The SACC will provide recommendations to inform EPA's final risk determinations and subsequent risk management actions.
events.why_relevant: This peer review process is a critical procedural step in EPA's regulatory authority under TSCA to assess chemical safety and determine whether phthalates present unreasonable risks to human health or the environment, potentially leading to restrictions or bans on widely used industrial chemicals.
events.basis: EPA is announcing that there will be two virtual public meetings of the Science Advisory Committee on Chemicals (SACC)... to consider the draft risk evaluations and technical support documents... The draft risk evaluations were prepared under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA).

events.title: EPA finalizes pesticide tolerance exemptions for capric, caprylic, and pelargonic acids
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency finalized a rule removing redundant pesticide tolerance limits and exemptions for three fatty acids (capric, caprylic, and pelargonic acids) used as antimicrobial treatments on food-contact surfaces. The rule consolidates existing tolerances under 40 CFR 180.940, 180.1159, and 180.1225, eliminating duplicate numerical limits while maintaining exemptions from tolerance requirements for these low-toxicity substances. The action implements registration review decisions and takes effect immediately, with a six-month transition period (through December 10, 2025) for affected producers.
events.why_relevant: This rule clarifies and streamlines federal pesticide residue standards, reducing regulatory redundancy while maintaining food safety protections for antimicrobial treatments in commercial food processing.
events.basis: EPA is removing the redundant exemptions and limits for capric (decanoic) acid under 40 CFR 180.940(b) and (c) entirely, removing the 100 ppm limit for capric (decanoic) acid from 40 CFR 180.940(a), and removing the limit of 170 ppm under 40 CFR 180.1225 for capric (decanoic) acid.

events.summary: Representative Sara Jacobs (California), Senator Mazie Hirono (Hawaii), and Senator Ron Wyden (Oregon) filed the "My Body, My Data" bill in both chambers of Congress on Wednesday. The legislation aims to prohibit companies from collecting, using, retaining, or disclosing reproductive health data—including information about pregnancy, menstruation, abortion, contraception—unless essential to providing a requested service. The bill responds to documented cases of law enforcement using data trails to identify abortion seekers, including Facebook chats used in Nebraska charges and cellphone location data deployed by anti-abortion activists.
events.why_relevant: The bill addresses a critical gap in federal privacy protections for reproductive health data in the post-Roe era, where law enforcement has already weaponized digital surveillance to prosecute abortion seekers and their families.
events.basis: Three Democratic members of Congress have introduced a bill to limit companies' ability to hoover up data about people's reproductive health…filed the 'my body, my data' bill in both the US House and Senate.

events.summary: In an interview with the Guardian, Senator Chris Murphy (D-CT) urges Democrats to embrace populism and focus on making work pay rather than offering subsidies, arguing the party has lost working-class voters. Murphy also warns that Trump is operating as a kleptocracy, enriching himself through foreign deals (Qatar's $400m jet gift, UAE semiconductor sales, Saudi nuclear technology exchanges) that pose national security risks. events.title: Federal judge blocks Trump citizenship-proof voting executive order
events.summary: Federal Judge Denise J. Casper in Massachusetts ruled that Democratic state attorneys general had a reasonable likelihood of success challenging provisions of Trump's executive order requiring proof of citizenship to vote. Casper granted an injunction blocking implementation of the order's requirement that local elections officials assess citizenship before distributing voter registration forms at public assistance agencies. This is the second federal judge to reject parts of the order, following an April ruling by a DC judge. The order, issued in March, had prompted multiple lawsuits from voting rights groups and Democratic officials.
events.why_relevant: The ruling protects voting access by blocking an executive order that would impose citizenship documentation requirements beyond statutory authority, directly affecting millions of voters' ability to register.
events.basis: A second federal judge has rejected parts of Donald Trump's executive order on elections, dealing another blow to his directive that would require proof of citizenship to vote in US elections.

events.title: Federal judge rules Trump administration cannot detain Mahmoud Khalil on foreign policy threat basis
events.summary: Federal Judge Michael E. Farbiarz ruled Wednesday that the Trump administration cannot detain Columbia University graduate and Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil based on Secretary of State Marco Rubio's determination that he poses a threat to U.S. foreign policy. The order takes effect Friday at 9:30 a.m., though Khalil may remain detained on separate grounds—alleged inaccuracies in his green card application. Khalil, arrested in March without a warrant, has been held in Louisiana since then and was the first student arrested in the administration's crackdown on pro-Palestinian campus activism.
events.why_relevant: The ruling constrains executive detention authority based on political speech and foreign policy disagreement, establishing judicial limits on the administration's use of immigration detention as a tool to suppress activism.
events.basis: A federal judge has ruled that the Trump administration can no longer detain the Columbia University graduate and Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil on the basis of federal claims that he is a threat to US foreign policy.

events.title: Complaint filed — Al Otro Lado v. Trump (S.D. Cal. 3:25-cv-01501)
events.summary: Al Otro Lado and Haitian Bridge Alliance, two immigration nonprofits, filed a class action complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California challenging Executive Order 10888, issued January 20, 2025. The EO bars immigrants arriving after its date from invoking Immigration and Nationality Act provisions permitting them to remain in the U.S. while pursuing asylum claims. Plaintiffs allege the EO violates 8 U.S.C. § 1158 by unlawfully shutting down asylum access at U.S.-Mexico border ports of entry, violates the Administrative Procedure Act as arbitrary and capricious, and exceeds executive authority. Plaintiffs seek a declaration that the EO and asylum blockade are unlawful and an injunction against implementation.
events.why_relevant: The lawsuit directly challenges executive authority to restrict asylum access and raises fundamental questions about separation of powers, statutory interpretation, and administrative procedure.

events.title: Trump DOJ issues memo directing denaturalization of naturalized citizens for criminal offenses
events.summary: The Trump administration's Justice Department published a memo on June 11, 2025, directing federal attorneys to prioritize civil proceedings to revoke U.S. citizenship from naturalized citizens who "illegally procured" naturalization or obtained it through "concealment of a material fact or willful misrepresentation." The memo targets an estimated 25 million naturalized citizens and lists 10 priority categories for denaturalization, including those convicted of crimes. Critically, those in civil denaturalization proceedings are denied the right to an attorney and face a lower burden of proof than in criminal cases. The directive expands discretion to pursue denaturalization for immigration form fraud, financial fraud, medical fraud, and cases referred by U.S. attorneys or connected to pending criminal charges.
events.why_relevant: This policy creates a two-tiered citizenship system, strips constitutional protections from naturalized Americans, and weaponizes denaturalization as a tool of political control by lowering procedural safeguards and expanding prosecutorial discretion.
events.basis: The memo, published on 11 June, calls on attorneys in the department to institute civil proceedings to revoke a person's United States citizenship if an individual either 'illegally procured' naturalization or procured naturalization by 'concealment of a material fact or by willful misrepresentation'.

The submission includes revisions to three Cluster Report Forms (Initial, Follow-up, and Annual/Closeout) designed to streamline data collection, reduce respondent burden, and improve data quality. The CDC is requesting a 30-day public comment period and three-year OMB approval. Total estimated annualized burden is 60,731 hours across 59 state and territorial health departments.
events.why_relevant: Public comment periods on federal information collection requests are a mechanism for democratic input into regulatory burden and data governance affecting state health agencies and public health surveillance.
events.basis: CDC has submitted the information collection request titled 'National HIV Surveillance System (NHSS)' to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval.

events.title: CDC Submits National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System for Paperwork Reduction Act Review
events.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention submitted the "National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System" information collection request to the Office of Management and Budget for review under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. The revision seeks three-year approval to receive case notification data for three new conditions—Chagas disease, yersiniosis (non-pestis), and firearm-related injuries—and new disease-specific data elements for toxoplasmosis. CDC opens a 30-day public comment period; the estimated annual burden is 18,354 hours across 257 respondents in state, territorial, local, and freely associated jurisdictions.
events.why_relevant: Expansion of disease surveillance data collection affects public health transparency, data governance, and the administrative burden on state and local health departments that feed national disease monitoring systems.
events.basis: CDC has submitted the information collection request titled 'National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System' to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval.

events.title: Federal appeals court stays judge's order returning California National Guard to Newsom

events.summary: The Trump administration is pursuing significant reductions to the US National Park Service's stewardship budget, cutting it from approximately $375 million to $185 million. events.title: US appeals court denies Trump's challenge to $5m E Jean Carroll defamation damages award

events.title: EPA finalizes significant new use rules for 34 chemical substances under TSCA
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency issued final Significant New Use Rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act for 34 chemical substances previously subject to premanufacture notices. The determination spans from December 19, 2013 (investigational exemption effective date) through February 5, 2021 (approval date). This establishes the maximum potential patent extension period; the applicant seeks 137–179 days of actual extension. Public comment period closes August 19, 2025; petitions on due diligence due by December 17, 2025.
events.why_relevant: Patent term extension determinations affect pharmaceutical innovation incentives, market exclusivity periods, and drug pricing dynamics—core elements of regulatory and economic policy affecting public health access and industry competition.
events.basis: FDA has determined that the applicable regulatory review period for BREYANZI is 2,607 days. Of this time, 2,191 days occurred during the testing phase of the regulatory review period, while 416 days occurred during the approval phase.

events.title: President grants presidential permit to City of Laredo, Texas to expand and operate vehicular border crossing at Laredo-Colombia Solidarity International Bridge.
events.summary: The President issued a Presidential Permit on June 13, 2025, authorizing the City of Laredo, Texas to expand and continue operating a vehicular crossing at the Laredo-Colombia Solidarity International Bridge Land Port of Entry on the U.S.-Mexico border. The permit authorizes construction of two new 4-lane spans for commercial traffic parallel to the existing bridge. The permittee must comply with all federal, state, and local laws; obtain required environmental permits; provide inspection facilities and infrastructure at no cost to the U.S.; and obtain State Department diplomatic clearance from Mexico before commencing construction. The permit expires in 5 years if construction has not begun and remains in effect only while operations continue.
events.why_relevant: Presidential permits for international border infrastructure affect cross-border commerce, trade capacity, and bilateral relations with Mexico, and establish conditions for federal oversight of critical border facilities.
events.basis: I hereby grant permission, subject to the conditions set forth herein, to the City of Laredo, Texas (the 'permittee'), to expand and continue to maintain and operate a vehicular crossing at the Laredo-Colombia Solidarity International Bridge Land Port of Entry.

events.title: Director of National Portrait Gallery resigns after Trump's effort to fire her
events.summary: Kim Sajet, director of the National Portrait Gallery since 2013, resigned on June 13 after Donald Trump announced her firing on May 30, citing her as "highly partisan" and a "strong supporter of DEI." The Smithsonian Institution's board of regents had rebuffed Trump's attempt to remove her, asserting its independent governance authority. Sajet's departure came after a two-week standoff in which she continued working despite Trump's public dismissal announcement. Kevin Gover was named acting director.

events.title: Republicans and Trump praise Israeli strikes on Iran; Democrats warn of sabotaged nuclear talks
events.summary: Donald Trump and Republican leaders including Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Speaker Mike Johnson publicly praised Israel's military strikes on Iran on Friday. Several Democrats, including Senators Chris Murphy and Tim Kaine, accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of deliberately ordering the strikes to sabotage ongoing U.S.-Iran nuclear negotiations scheduled for the weekend. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated U.S. forces were not involved; Trump suggested Iran had "perhaps, a second chance" to negotiate. The strikes occurred amid heightened tensions over Trump's deployment of federalized National Guard troops to Los Angeles and the detention of Senator Alex Padilla by federal agents.
events.why_relevant: The strikes and political response reveal deep divisions over U.S. foreign policy toward Iran, with Republicans backing military action while Democrats argue it undermines diplomatic efforts and risks regional escalation that threatens American security interests.

events.title: Trump administration deploys US Marines and National Guard to Los Angeles against state wishes
events.summary: Following protests against immigration raids in the LA area, the Trump administration deployed US Marines and the National Guard to Los Angeles to guard immigration enforcement operations, acting against California's explicit objections. events.title: US Marines detain civilian outside federal building in Los Angeles
events.summary: US Marines deployed to Los Angeles by Trump temporarily detained Marcos Leao, a 27-year-old Army veteran and US citizen, outside the Wilshire Federal Building on June 13. Leao was restrained with zip ties and transferred to Department of Homeland Security custody after crossing a taped-off area. Military Northern Command confirmed active-duty forces "may temporarily detain an individual in specific circumstances," with detention ending when transfer to civilian law enforcement occurs. Leao reported being treated fairly after release.
events.why_relevant: This marks the first known detention by active-duty federal troops deployed domestically in response to protests, raising constitutional concerns about military involvement in civilian law enforcement and suppression of dissent.
events.basis: US marines deployed to Los Angeles on Friday temporarily detained a civilian, the US military confirmed, in the first known detention by active-duty troops deployed there by Donald Trump.
